venue.name: B.C. Aviation Museum
venue.description: The British Columbia Aviation Museum sits on the south-east corner of the Victoria International Airport lands in North Saanich and displays the Hawaii Mars water bomber along with over 40 aircraft, engines, models and artefacts from British Columbia and Canadian aviation history. A children's area in the Main Hangar holds plane pedal carts, flight simulators, interactive aircraft and hands-on aviation themed displays. The museum runs curriculum-linked education programs from preschool to secondary and also offers guided tours for all ages.
venue.address: 1910 Norseman Road, North Saanich, B.C. V8L 5V5

facility_notes.bus_parking: Free parking located on premises. Oversized vehicles are permitted in our Additional Parking Lot area only.

restrictions: Children under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an adult.
Children must be supervised at all times. Museum staff and volunteers are not to be asked to supervise children.
Video recording of Museum programs and commercial photography are not permitted within the Museum, unless authorized by the Executive Director or Museum President.
Smoking is not permitted anywhere within the gated property of the BC Aviation Museum.
Dogs are allowed everyday BUT WEDNESDAY. Due to Volunteer, Staff and Patron allergies, Wednesday is a DOG FREE day.
venue.seasonal_notes: Holiday hours: December 24th OPEN from 10 AM to 4:00 PM, December 25th CLOSED, December 26th CLOSED, December 31st OPEN from 10AM to 4:00 PM, January 1st CLOSED. No administrative staff available between December 25th and January 2nd. Access to the inside of the Hawaii Mars is weather dependent to ensure the safety of our visitors.

programs.name: Hands-On Flying with Models (Preschool to Grade 1)
programs.description: Curriculum-linked museum program for preschool to Grade 1 classes. Students are introduced to selected Museum displays and challenged to determine how an airplane is able to fly, then each build a glider and experiment with the properties that influence flight. Booked as a morning visit (10am to 12pm) or an afternoon visit (12:30pm to 2:30pm).
programs.what_children_do: Look at selected museum displays and work out what an aeroplane needs in order to fly, then build a glider each and experiment with the properties that change how it flies.
programs.our_note: The slot is fixed: the museum will not run past your booked block if the bus is late, and it asks groups not to arrive more than 15 minutes early because the entry area cannot hold a class. In fair weather it expects groups to wait in the front garden until start time.
programs.practical_summary: The museum is wheelchair accessible, parking on site is free and adult supervisors are admitted free. Washrooms, indoor lunch space, maximum group size and the minimum booking notice are not stated on the site, so ask when you email.
programs.payment_timing: You will be invoiced prior to your visit to the museum. Payment is due on the day of the visit.
programs.cancellation_note: Cancellations must be made at least 72 hours prior to your scheduled program. All rescheduled programs must be given at least one week in advance. Cancellations made inside the 72-hour window will be subject to a 50% cancellation fee.
programs.evidence: Pricing for these types of visits is set at $8.50 per student, with no charge for adult supervisors.

programs.name: The Science of Flight – Bernoulli's Principals (Grades 6/7)
programs.description: Curriculum-linked museum program for Grade 6 and 7 classes exploring how flight is possible in a world of gravity. Students are introduced to Bernoulli's Principal and the effect of balanced and unbalanced forces, conduct an experiment to see it in action, then use museum displays to reinforce what they discovered. Booked as a morning visit (10am to 12pm) or an afternoon visit (12:30pm to 2:30pm); the published rate is $8.50 per student with no charge for adult supervisors.
programs.what_children_do: Learn Bernoulli's Principal, then run an experiment to see it in action before going back out to the museum displays to check what they found.
programs.our_note: Two hours with an experiment in the middle, so it suits a class that can settle for a sit-down segment. The museum will not extend the block for a late arrival and charges in full for no-shows.
programs.practical_summary: The museum is wheelchair accessible, parking on site is free and adult supervisors are admitted free. Washrooms, indoor lunch space, maximum group size and the minimum booking notice are not stated on the site, so ask when you email.

programs.name: The History of the Commonwealth Air Training Program (Grades 11/12)
programs.description: Curriculum-linked museum program for Grade 11 and 12 classes on Canada's contribution to the Second World War through the Commonwealth Air Training Plan. Students examine its role before, during and after the war, view selected museum displays, answer thought-provoking questions about the Plan and then debate their responses with their peers. Booked as a morning visit (10am to 12pm) or an afternoon visit (12:30pm to 2:30pm); the published rate is $8.50 per student with no charge for adult supervisors.
programs.what_children_do: Work through selected museum displays answering questions about the Commonwealth Air Training Plan, then debate their answers with their classmates.
programs.our_note: This one is discussion-led, so it needs a group willing to argue a point in a public gallery. Note the museum's own rule that under-16s must be accompanied by an adult still applies.
programs.practical_summary: The museum is wheelchair accessible, parking on site is free and adult supervisors are admitted free. Washrooms, indoor lunch space, maximum group size and the minimum booking notice are not stated on the site, so ask when you email.

programs.name: Guided museum tour
programs.description: A guided tour with one of the museum's specially trained guides. Students explore the exhibits, learning about the history of aviation in British Columbia and Canada, and have the opportunity to walk through selected aircraft, from sitting in the pilot's seat of a Lockheed T-33 Fighter Jet to walking through the Hawaii Mars Waterbomber. The site says tours are offered for all ages but does not publish a price, duration or capacity for a tour-only group booking.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the exhibits with a guide and go inside selected aircraft, including sitting in the pilot's seat of a Lockheed T-33 fighter jet and walking through the Hawaii Mars water bomber.
programs.our_note: Ask what a tour on its own costs a group. The $8.50 per student rate is written for the booked education programs, and the only group price the site publishes elsewhere is an adult group rate for ten or more prebooked visitors.
programs.practical_summary: The museum is wheelchair accessible with free parking on site. Price, length and group size for a tour-only visit are not published, and washrooms and lunch space are not mentioned anywhere on the site.
programs.evidence: The museum offers guided tours for all ages.

programs.name: Hawaii Mars Flight Deck Tour
programs.description: A 45-minute guided look at the Hawaii Mars and its flight deck, offered every Saturday at 11am and 1pm for ages 12+. Places are limited and first-come, first-served; the museum does not accept pre-bookings, so this cannot be reserved for a class. Tours are weather dependent and will be cancelled due to inclement weather.
programs.what_children_do: Go up on to the flight deck of the Hawaii Mars water bomber with a guide for a 45-minute close look at the aircraft and its cockpit.
programs.our_note: Not bookable ahead and $25 a head, so treat it as an add-on a few older students might queue for rather than something you can build a trip around. Ask on the day whether the weather has cancelled it.
programs.practical_summary: Runs only on Saturdays and only for ages 12 and over, with no pre-booking and no group rate published. Washrooms and lunch space are not mentioned anywhere on the site.
programs.cancellation_note: Flight Deck Tours are weather dependent; tours will be cancelled due to inclement weather.
programs.evidence: Tours are $25 per person on a first-come, first-served basis.

values: Open Daily, from 10 AM to 4 PM
The BC Aviation Museum is open from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM, 7 days a week, September to June. 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM, July to August.
conflicts.note: The homepage and the site footer give a single year-round 10 AM to 4 PM opening, while the Visit page publishes seasonal hours with a 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM summer schedule for July and August. Neither page is dated, so hours_notes is left null.
